text:
jessica: Hey team, customer T-420 opened an escalation — streaming responses cut off after ~90s, client reconnects and we see duplicate billing events. Repro steps attached.

alex: Can you paste the raw client logs / headers?

jessica: From their frontend: 
```
GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-alpha HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Connection: keep-alive
Accept: text/event-stream
```
Client logs show: "stream ended unexpectedly, reconnecting (code ECONNRESET)" after ~92s.

ingrid: What LB in front of them? ALB/NLB/Cloudflare?

jessica: They're on ALB in front of nginx (customer architecture). They also routed through Cloudflare in some tests.

alex: Similar to previous idle-probe races, could be ALB idle timeout (default 60s) vs nginx upstream keepalive vs our SSE chunk trigger. But 92s is odd. Any evidence of partial buffers (trailing commas or missing final chunk)?

jessica: They see partial JSON objects streamed then silence, then reconnect. No 502. Our logs show connection closed from client side. Token refresh happens on reconnect and billing increments per reconnect.

ops-oncall: Can we get a server-side TCP dump from customer? Also need our side load balancer metrics: connection_close reasons and bytes sent.

jessica: Customer sent tcpdump excerpt (trimmed):
```
... GET ... 0-90s streaming data chunks every 1s ... then client FIN at 92s
```
No RST from upstream.

ingrid: Interesting. Could be Cloudflare buffering/coalescing hidden keepalive probes. Did they test bypassing Cloudflare?

jessica: Yes — bypassed CF and still reproduced. They tried direct ALB->nginx and also nginx->app. Repro only when nginx proxy buffering is enabled. With `proxy_buffering off;` the problem disappears.

alex: Aha. That suggests nginx is aggregating chunks until a buffer threshold or timeout then writing in a burst which confuses client keepalive or the client's SSE parser. Which nginx version? And what's proxy_buffers/timeout settings?

jessica: nginx 1.20.1. Config snippet they sent: 
```
proxy_buffering on;
proxy_buffers 8 16k;
proxy_busy_buffers_size 32k;
proxy_read_timeout 90s; # default changed by infra team
```
They increased `proxy_read_timeout` to 90s.

ops-oncall: There's the smoking gun: proxy_read_timeout at 90s can cause nginx to close backends after that period of inactivity on the response body. If our runtime keeps sending small SSE chunks but nginx considers them buffered and not flushed, the backend->nginx stream looks idle and nginx hits the 90s read timeout, closing the connection. Client sees silence then reconnect. When buffering is off, nginx flushes every chunk so it stays active.

alex: So two paths: 1) recommend `proxy_buffering off` or `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection \"\";` and `chunked_transfer_encoding on;` 2) increase `proxy_read_timeout` > 180s and tune `proxy_buffers` to avoid aggregation. Also ensure `X-Accel-Buffering: no` can be set by app for per-response control.

jessica: Customer tried adding `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and that fixed it in staging. They prefer not to change global nginx settings across apps.

billing-ops: How do we prevent duplicate billing for reconnects? Can we debounce billing per session id?

alex: We bill per completed token stream event currently. For reconnects we record new session id and bill again. Short term: add a debounce window (e.g., 2 minutes) keyed by client session id or initial request id so rapid reconnects don't double-bill. Long term: server should honor `Idempotency-Key` header and tie billing to that.

ops-oncall: For support reply: outline repro steps, mitigation (X-Accel-Buffering: no), recommended nginx settings, and offer a backend change to support idempotency-key billing debounce. Also escalate to infra to add a docs note about SSE + nginx buffering.

jessica: Draft reply to customer: 
"Thanks — root cause appears to be nginx proxy_buffering + proxy_read_timeout=90s causing backend->proxy perceived idle when buffered. Short-term options: set response header `X-Accel-Buffering: no` in your app or set `proxy_buffering off;` for the SSE location. Alternatively increase `proxy_read_timeout` to > 180s and tune proxy_buffers. We can also implement billing debounce on our side to avoid duplicate charges from quick reconnects. Let us know if you'd like us to help patch the app to set the header." :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: Deployed patch `billing-debounce-v0.1` to staging (runbook: feature-flag off by default).

billing-ops: Please monitor staging billing for false-negatives.

ingrid: Add an RFC/KB: "SSE and reverse proxies (nginx/ALB/Cloudflare) — buffering and idle timeout interactions" with example configs and the `X-Accel-Buffering` tip.

jessica: Customer confirmed staging fix works. Moving to customer confirm and billing credit discussion. Closing loop after billing-debounce flag tested.

alex: Great triage. TL;DR: nginx proxy_buffering + short proxy_read_timeout caused backend perceived idleness despite app streaming; fix = disable buffering per-response or raise timeout; add server-side billing debounce as safety net.

jessica: I'll update the ticket and mark as Escalation -> Resolved once billing credits are agreed.
